title: Increase in Fake Bulk Order Scams Impersonating SAF Personnel and Measures to Protect Small Businesses
what_it_is: Increase in Fake Bulk Order Scams Impersonating SAF Personnel and Measures to Protect Small Businesses

sections.label: Fake SAF bulk order scams
sections.summary: From May to 15 September 2025, Police received at least six reports of scammers posing as SAF personnel to make bulk orders and direct victims to pay fake suppliers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam
sentences.text: From May 2025 to 15 September 2025, the Police received at least six reports of fake bulk order scams involving the impersonation of Singapore Armed Forces (SAF) personnel.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam
sentences.text: In these scams, scammers posing as SAF personnel would contact restaurants or other small businesses to make bulk orders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam
sentences.text: The scammers would then provide the contact details of fake suppliers whom they claim can supply the additional items and persuade the victims to pay these fake suppliers on their behalf.

sections.label: Arrests in fake order scams
sections.summary: As of 19 September 2025, Police arrested six suspects, including a 22-year-old woman charged on 17 September for relinquishing her bank account to scammers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam
sentences.text: As of 19 September 2025, the Police have arrested six suspects in connection with these scams.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam
sentences.text: Amongst them is a 22-year-old woman who was charged in court on 17 September for relinquishing control of her bank account to the scammers to facilitate the scams.

sections.label: Police scam awareness for businesses
sections.summary: Police shared scam signs and preventive measures with industry stakeholders, urging businesses to verify identities, avoid advance payments, and pay on delivery.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam
sentences.text: To raise awareness of fake bulk order scams among small businesses, the Police have been sharing with industry stakeholders such as the Food and Beverage Management Association Singapore, Restaurant Association of Singapore and Orchard Road Business Association the telltale signs of scams and the preventive measures they should adopt.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam
sentences.text: In particular, we urge businesses to try to verify the identity of the people they are transacting with, avoid making advance payments or deposits with new suppliers, and pay only upon the delivery of goods.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam
sentences.text: Please note also that Government agencies will not ask businesses to make payment to another business on the Government’s behalf, unless agreed through a written contract.
